## Summary

- `pnpm build` fails on `@rivet-dev/agent-os-opencode` with `error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen` from `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Root cause: upstream `packages/app/package.json` (in the v1.3.13 source tarball) pins `"ghostty-web": "github:anomalyco/ghostty-web#main"` — a moving branch ref — while the bundled `bun.lock` snapshots commit `4af877d`. Once `main` advances (currently `20bd361`), frozen-lockfile install can no longer satisfy resolution.
- Fix: between tarball extraction and `bun install`, rewrite the `ghostty-web` ref in `packages/app/package.json` to the SHA the lockfile already records (`4af877d`). `--frozen-lockfile` is preserved, so any drift on either side still fails loudly — we're not silently absorbing whatever new HEAD `main` advances to (which would be a supply-chain footgun if that branch were force-pushed or compromised).

body:
## Summary

Fixes two independent bugs. The primary change splits `findDueCardsOn` into separate review-card and new-card LIMIT windows so a large backlog of never-reviewed cards can no longer crowd out overdue FSRS reviews. A secondary change wraps the `schema_migrations` RLS migration statements in `to_regclass` guards so the migration becomes a no-op in non-golang-migrate harnesses (e.g. the SchemaSpy ER-chart workflow) where the table is absent.

## Background / Motivation

- `findDueCardsOn` used a single `COALESCE(ucs.due, cards.created_at) ASC` ORDER BY across all candidate cards. New cards with old `created_at` values sort before FSRS-due review cards with newer `due` timestamps, so a cardgroup with many unreviewed cards would fill the LIMIT with new cards and silently skip overdue reviews — making FSRS scheduling appear inert on large cardgroups.
- Migration `20260603090000_enable_rls_schema_migrations` ran `ALTER TABLE public.schema_migrations` unconditionally. The table is created by golang-migrate at runtime, not by any SQL file, so harnesses that apply migrations directly with `psql` (e.g. the SchemaSpy ER-chart job in `.github/workflows/`) would error on a non-existent table.

## Changes

### Repository: dual-fetch fix (`card.go`)

- `findDueCardsOn` now runs two independent LIMIT queries: review cards (`ucs.due IS NOT NULL AND ucs.due <= now`) ordered by `ucs.due ASC`, and new cards (`ucs.due IS NULL`) ordered by `cards.created_at ASC`. Slices are concatenated and forwarded to `OrderingPolicy.Apply` for the final interleave and per-session truncation.
- Extracted `dueRowsOn` (shared JOIN/SELECT/LIMIT builder) and `dueCardsFromRows` (NULL → `FSRSStateNew` mapper) so the SELECT and JOIN cannot drift between the two fetches.

### Migration guard (`20260603090000_enable_rls_schema_migrations`)

- Both `.up.sql` and `.down.sql` now open with `IF to_regclass('public.schema_migrations') IS NULL THEN RAISE NOTICE ...; RETURN; END IF;` so the entire block is a no-op when the table is absent.
- All `ALTER TABLE` / `REVOKE` / `GRANT` statements inside the block use `EXECUTE` (dynamic SQL), required by PostgreSQL for conditional DDL.

### Tests

- `TestCardRepository_FindDueCards_ReviewsNotStarvedByNewBacklog`: 5 new cards with old `created_at` + 2 now-due review cards + `limit=3` → asserts both review cards are present in the result regardless of the new-card backlog size.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/repository/... -race -run TestCardRepository_FindDueCards_ReviewsNotStarvedByNewBacklog` → PASS
- `go test ./internal/database/... -race` → PASS (down/up roundtrip exercises the `to_regclass` guard path)

## Test plan

- [ ] `go build ./...` passes
- [ ] `go vet ./...` clean
- [ ] `go test ./internal/repository/... -race` → PASS (includes new starvation regression test)
- [ ] `go test ./internal/database/... -race` → PASS (migration roundtrip for the guarded migration)
- [ ] In a cardgroup with 10+ new cards and 2 now-due review cards, confirm the review cards appear in the learn session when limit ≤ 5

author: camsoper
body:
## What happened
A manual dispatch of the weekly digest (run [#26856266206](https://github.com/pulumi/docs/actions/runs/26856266206)) wedged on the **Post digest to Slack** step and had to be cancelled. The job logs show the root cause:

```
00:31:10  Run uv run scripts/weekly-digest/post-to-slack.py ...
00:38:40  post attempt 1 failed (<urlopen error timed out>); retrying in 2s
00:39:30  ##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

A **single** `chat.postMessage` attempt took ~7.5 minutes to time out despite a 30s timeout. `slack.com` resolves to both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and Python's `socket.create_connection` tries them **sequentially with no Happy Eyeballs** — on a runner without IPv6 egress, each unreachable IPv6 address burns the full socket timeout before falling through, stacking far past the per-request budget. The link checker doesn't hit this because `@slack/web-api` races addresses in parallel.

The exception handling itself worked (it caught the timeout and was retrying) — the problems were the per-attempt latency and the absence of any hard ceiling.

## Fix
- **`post-to-slack.py`** — drop `AF_INET6` from resolution so we only dial IPv4, cut the per-request timeout to 10s, and catch `OSError` (covers socket timeouts and connection resets, not just `URLError`) so transient failures retry cleanly. An `ok:false` from Slack still fails fast.
- **`weekly-digest.yml`** — add `timeout-minutes: 3` to the post step as a hard ceiling, so a stuck post can never hold the runner for the default 6 hours again.

## Validation
- After `_force_ipv4()`, `getaddrinfo("slack.com", 443)` returns only `AF_INET`; chunker and `--dry-run` unaffected; `py_compile` + YAML parse clean.
- The live `chat.postMessage` path still only runs in CI. Recommend a real `workflow_dispatch` on this branch to confirm the post now completes in seconds.

Follow-up consideration (not in this PR): for full parity with the link checker we could move posting to Node + `@slack/web-api`, which gets Happy Eyeballs and retries for free. The IPv4 pin above is the smaller, targeted fix for the observed failure.

author: lnds
body:
## What

Adds the **port/effect form** of the Repository, alongside the existing value form, closing a gap in henua v0.1.

henua shipped the Repository only as a **value** (`InMemoryRepository` threaded explicitly through `save`/`find`/`delete`). That is the weaker shape for ports-and-adapters: the domain's signature names the *concrete* repository type, so it depends on the adapter, not only on the port — closer to a hand-passed service locator than to a late-bound port.

This PR adds the form with the full hexagonal property:

- **The port** — `effect Repository[a, i]` (`find` / `save` / `delete`), parametric over the aggregate `a` and id `i`. A domain function declares `/ Repository[a, i]` in its row and is **structurally incapable** of naming a concrete repository.
- **The adapter** — the enclosing handler. `with_in_memory` / `with_in_memory_seeded` install an in-memory handler built **on the value form's `Map` logic** (reused, not reimplemented — the only difference is who threads the state). kohau-backed `with_sqlite` / `with_postgres` are future adapters.
- The effect-row checker **enforces the dependency rule** the value form left to discipline.

The two forms are **layers, not competitors** (Decision 9): value form for pure threading / tests / fixtures and as the adapter's substrate; effect form for compiler-checked, late-bound ports. This matches the two-shape discipline ahu and kohau already pin ("pure form for tests / wrapped form for production"), and it is the surface `manutara` targets so a route's effect row inherits persistence access.

## Why an effect succeeds where Decision 1 said a protocol fails

A protocol is single-dispatch on `Self` and pure; an effect **is** an effect row and is parametric over `(a, i)` — exactly the axis of variation Decision 1 identified. `effect Repository[a, i]` with ops returning generic `Option[a]` / `Bool` is verified to compile and run against kai 0.84.0 and 0.86.1.

## Contents

- `henua/repository_effect.kai` — the `Repository[a, i]` effect + in-memory adapter
- `tests/repository_effect_roundtrip.kai` (+ golden) — tier1 fixture
- `examples/repository_port/` — the same domain run under two adapters (in-memory vs a tracing "driver"), showing zero domain change
- `docs/design.md` — **Decision 9**, a clarifying note on Decision 1, Status + §*The surface* updates (six → seven modules)

## Testing

`make tier1-pure` green: 10 pure fixtures, the new `repository_effect_roundtrip` included, no regressions to existing fixtures.

## Notes

- No `VERSION` / `CHANGELOG` bump (integrator assigns post-merge).
- The fallible-adapter error story (infrastructure failures via a `Fail`-shaped effect on the adapter's own row) and the first kohau-backed `with_sqlite` adapter are explicit v0.2 follow-ups, noted in Decision 9.

author: jedi12many
body:
> one of the common problems is space on our worker nodes. logs fill up space over time. can we flag that?

Yes — and it's the **root cause** of the evicted pods from before: logs fill the disk → the kubelet trips **`DiskPressure`** → it starts evicting. So flagging node conditions catches the cause, not just the symptom.

```
steadystate> probe prod
  HIGH   node ip-10-0-1-5 has DiskPressure on prod-cluster
         kubelet has disk pressure
         fp 4f72305e...
```

- Reads each node's `status.conditions` (**one `kubectl get nodes -o json`** — cheap, always-on) and raises a **HIGH `Node` Symptom** for any node with **`DiskPressure`** / `MemoryPressure` / `PIDPressure` = True, or **`Ready` != True** (NotReady/down).
- Just another Symptom, so it inherits everything: state lifecycle (**resolves when the pressure clears**), `mute`, `show <fp>`, `--to servicenow`/Slack, `scan --json`. Identity is **context-qualified** (`<cluster>/Node/<name>`) so the same node name across clusters stays distinct, and per-node so you see *which* node.
- **Locked-down-friendly:** `get nodes` is basic cluster-scoped RBAC — far more likely permitted in your locked-down clusters than the `nodes/proxy` metrics endpoint a proactive %-full check needs. A denied/failed read degrades to no node symptoms, never crashes the scan.

### Tests
`node_issues` flags pressure + NotReady and skips healthy nodes; the probe raises a HIGH `Node` DiskPressure symptom with a context-qualified identity; the node read is best-effort (denied/failed → nothing). 997 passed, 7 skipped; ruff + format + mypy clean.

### Caveat / follow-up
`DiskPressure` fires *at* the eviction threshold (reactive — disk already ~full). A **proactive "node is N% full" early warning** needs actual usage %, which means the kubelet **summary API** (`nodes/proxy`, per-node calls) — a natural follow-up for clusters that grant it. Node conditions are the reliable, works-everywhere signal; happy to add the proactive version if your RBAC allows `nodes/proxy`.

author: afonsopc
body:
## Summary
_decode_header in mcp_servers/email_server.py joins the parts returned by email.header.decode_header with " ". But decode_header returns plain-text runs WITH their own surrounding whitespace, e.g. (b'Re: ', None), so every non-ASCII subject renders like "Re:  Jose" (double space) and senders like "=?utf-8?b?...?= <jose@x.com>" gain a stray space. It also violates RFC 2047 section 6.2: whitespace between two adjacent encoded-words must be dropped, so mixed-charset runs like Café + 日本 render with a bogus space in the middle. This is what every list/read/search tool result shows the model.

## Fix
Use the stdlib email.header.make_header, which concatenates correctly for all three cases, with a lossy per-part fallback for malformed headers or unknown charsets.

## Changes
- mcp_servers/email_server.py: _decode_header uses make_header with a safe fallback.
- tests/test_mcp_email_decode_header_spaces.py: prefix+encoded-word, encoded-word+name, adjacent mixed-charset words (all fail on old code), plain ASCII and empty header regressions.

A task original assumia **Next.js 15 (App Router)**, mas o projeto é **Vite + React 18 + React Router DOM 6** (template `vite_react_shadcn_ts`, `vercel.json` com `"framework": "vite"`). Nada de `app/layout.tsx`, `@next/third-parties`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts` ou `next/script` é aplicável.

author: heyong4725
body:
## Problem

Closes #1999.

`Daemon::run()` calls `set_up_event_stream` on every (re)connect, and that function bound the dynamic-node listener on `local_listen_port` each time. On a reconnect:

- The listener task from the previous connection is still running and still holds the port (it's a detached `tokio::spawn`, never aborted) — leaked.
- The rebind hits `AddrInUse`, so `spawn_listener_loop` returns `Ok(None)` (`local_listener.rs`) and the daemon **silently runs without a dynamic-node listener** for the rest of its life.

So after the first reconnect, dynamic nodes can no longer connect to the daemon, and every additional flap leaks another listener task. Static nodes are unaffected (ephemeral ports). Found during the #1998 review.

## Fix

Bind the dynamic-node listener **once**, before the reconnect loop, for the daemon's lifetime:

- `run()` binds the listener once and holds `dynamic_node_events_rx` for the whole loop, so the flume channel stays open across reconnect gaps.
- Each loop iteration streams a `clone()` of that receiver into the merged event stream (flume is MPMC; only the active clone-stream is polled, so dynamic-node events route to the current connection).
- `set_up_event_stream` now takes the receiver instead of a port and no longer binds.

The one-shot `run_dataflow` path (`dora daemon --run-dataflow`) binds its own listener once and has no reconnect loop, so it's unchanged.

## Verification (local, behavioral)

Forced a coordinator reconnect (kill + restart within the window):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Daemon re-registers after reconnect | ✅ |
| `"listen port already in use"` warnings (the leak symptom) | **0** (previously logged on every reconnect) |

Plus: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all` (excl. Python), `cargo check --examples` all pass.

Note: a full dynamic-node-across-reconnect e2e isn't part of the smoke suite (would need a dynamic-node harness); the leak symptom is eliminated and reconnection verified, and the listener is now bound for the daemon's lifetime so dynamic nodes survive reconnects.

body:
**Stacked on #1** (base = `fix/maintenance-automation-sprint0`). Merge #1 first, or merge this into #1.

## The core finding
The health functions already *detect* problems — `weekly-health-check` computes `critical_issues`, `generate-daily-ops-log` computes `brands_failed` + auto-generated `opportunities` — but they only **wrote to a table and stopped**. Nobody was alerted. That's why the freeze went unseen for weeks. This PR connects detection to a channel, and adds the external watchdog for the failure mode no in-workflow alert can catch.

## Changes (all additive, all no-op until secrets are set)
- **`_shared/notify.ts`** — fail-safe alert dispatch to `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`. Never throws; logs + no-ops when unset.
- **`weekly-health-check`** — alerts on `critical_issues` (pass-rate <80%, stale prices, missing stores).
- **`generate-daily-ops-log`** — alerts on failed brand syncs, `brands_synced == 0` (pipeline may be dead), or high-priority opportunities.
- **`sync-filaments` + `refresh-sitemaps`** — external dead-man-switch pings (`HEALTHCHECK_SYNC_URL` / `HEALTHCHECK_SITEMAPS_URL`). A monitor alerts when the expected ping **never arrives**.
- **`OPERATIONS.md`** — alerting-setup handoff, the **60-day auto-disable** warning, status updates.

## ⚠️ Likely real root cause to check now
GitHub **auto-disables scheduled workflows after 60 days of repo inactivity**. If `sync-filaments`/`refresh-sitemaps` were disabled, they stop running and emit **no alert** (summary/notify steps never execute). **Please check the Actions tab for a "this workflow was disabled" banner and re-enable** — this may be the actual freeze cause, independent of the #1 permissions bug.

## Operator setup to activate (after merge + deploy)
1. Set `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack/Discord/Hermes incoming webhook).
2. Create 2 healthchecks.io checks → set `HEALTHCHECK_SYNC_URL` (daily) + `HEALTHCHECK_SITEMAPS_URL` (weekly).
3. Deploy the two edge functions.

Edge functions edited but not deployed/run (no Supabase access yet). Logic is additive + fail-safe; needs a live run to confirm end-to-end.

body:
Adds `plan/rfc-frozen-render-world.md` recording the render-scaling investigation and the proposed architecture — explicitly **Draft / HOLD**, because the central bet is **unvalidated**.

**Robust findings:** the ~1.7–1.8x render plateau is a **2.6x parallel CPU inflation**; it is **not** lock contention (`cpu/wall=4.29` → cores busy), **not** allocation/GC (pure thread-local work scales 5.4x with 1.49x inflation, GC-independent), and is **associated with reading shared container objects** (shared-graph traversal inflates 4–6x).

**Why it's a HOLD:** cheap PoCs on Bengal's real data did **not** confirm a fix. `deepcopy`-owning the graph didn't help (strings aren't copied — they stay shared); `sys.intern()` (verified to *immortalize* on 3.14t) also didn't move traversal inflation (⇒ container, not string, contention) — yet owning containers didn't help either. Results were contradictory, and the decisive tool (`py-spy --native` refcount profiling) is **unsupported on macOS arm64**.

**Decision:** don't start the migration. Fund only **Step 0** (native profiling on Linux to name the dominant contended objects) + an isolation startup-amortization micro-benchmark. Re-open for approval once a single-step PoC shows a real `cpu/wall` drop with byte-identical output.

Plan-only change. The shipped correctness/measurement work (PR #301) stands regardless.

author: th0ma7
body: # imagecache: throttle & now-first ordering EPG sources that carry programme artwork expose hundreds of `` URLs. Tvheadend's imagecache fetches them on a single thread with **no pacing**, so on a guide grab it issues ~500 back-to-back HTTPS requests and the provider rate-limits/blocks the NAS IP (download failures in the log). > Serving the raw URL with imagecache disabled does **not** help: such providers also hotlink-protect by `Referer` — a browser `` sends `Referer` and gets `403`, while KODI/curl with no `Referer` get `200`. So caching server-side is the right path; it just must not hammer the source. These providers limit **images per IP per time window** (observed on tvtv.ca: ~50 per ~60 min). A failed request returns nothing and does **not** consume quota; the quota refills from the last **success**. So the sustainable rate is *"B images per T minutes"*, and the throttle's job is to learn `B` and `T` and then never exceed them. ## Changes ### Now-first ordering (always on) The fetch queue is sorted by a per-image priority instead of FIFO; EPG passes the programme start time so the visible "now" guide gets its images before far-future days (channel/dvr/rating icons keep priority 0). - New `imagecache_get_id_prio()`; `imagecache_get_id()` is a `prio=0` wrapper. - A shared image URL keeps the soonest priority and is re-sorted if still queued. - The thread always waits for the queue to be quiet (`IMAGECACHE_FETCH_SETTLE_MS`) before draining, so it drains a fully sorted queue rather than following a grab's (future-first) enqueue order. ### Download throttle — "Automatic download throttling" toggle (on by default) Kept in small helpers (`imagecache_throttle_*`) out of the fetch loop. - **Automatic — LEARN:** drain at full speed until blocked, then escalate a recovery pause up a ladder (5, 10, 15, 30, … min, kept strictly below the *Re-try period*) until a pause reliably refills the window — i.e. a window yields `>= IMAGECACHE_BATCH_MIN` images on `IMAGECACHE_LOCK_CONFIRM` tries **in a row**. Confirmation matters because one good window can be a fluke (the quota having refilled across earlier empty windows). That yields `B` (batch) and `T` (pause). - **Automatic — OPERATE:** on lock it computes the sustainable pace `ms = T/B` and drives a **token bucket** — one token every `ms`, capacity `~B` (with margin). A full bucket after idle lets a small update burst at full speed; a large queue drains at the sustainable rate and stops getting blocked. It logs the learned budget and, when a whole queued batch fits the budget, `M images queued, within budget -- full speed`. A block while operating re-learns one rung slower (any operating block counts toward that, cleared by a clean burst). - **Automatic — OPTIMIZE:** the learned `B per T` is a safe *lower* bound — the provider may sustain more if paced differently (the limit can be a mix of frequency and volume, not a flat count). After lock the throttle **binary-searches a faster pace**: it probes `ms/2` and, if that sustains `2×B` downloads **in a row** without a block, accepts it and probes faster; if a probe blocks first it takes one recovery pause and **bisects** between the fastest pace that failed and the slowest that held, converging on the fastest sustainable pace. Worst case it settles back on the learned `T/B`. The optimized pace is **persisted**, so a restart resumes there instead of re-probing. Each step logs (`probing N ms/image`, `N ms/image too fast`, `pace optimized -> N ms/image`). - **Manual (toggle off):** two now-visible fields, *Minimum delay between downloads (ms)* and *Back-off pause on blocking (minutes)*, used verbatim (`0/0` = no throttling). In automatic mode those are read-only (`get_opts`) and mirror the learned pace and pause. Saving the Image Cache config now logs the effective throttle setting (`config saved -- throttle manual, N ms/image, M min pause`), so a manual rate change is visible in the log. Only provider-block-like failures (`403`/`429`/`5xx`, timeout, dropped connection) count toward the back-off; a plain missing image (`404`/`410`) does **not**, so a few broken EPG URLs cannot trip a false block (`imagecache_image_fetch` now reports which it was). The **on-demand web fetch path** (`imagecache_filename`) shares the same provider budget instead of bypassing it. It still fetches **immediately** — the active user viewing the guide must not wait — but it **debits one token** from the bucket, so the background pacer waits one extra interval to repay it and the combined thread + on-demand rate stays within the provider window (previously an active client browsing the guide could silently overrun the window and trip an hour-long recovery pause). While a back-off pause is active it skips the fetch and serves a `404` (the thread gets the image afterwards); and if an on-demand fetch *itself* trips a block, it arms the recovery pause, voids the now-moot catch-up debt, and re-queues the image for the thread to retry — further on-demand requests are served `404` until the window refills. ### Reset button & completion log A **Reset auto-throttle** button on the Image Cache config toolbar (next to *Clean image cache* / *Re-fetch images*) drops the learned provider budget so the throttle re-learns from scratch: `imagecache_throttle_reset()` removes the persisted state and the fetch thread re-initialises (`api/imagecache/config/resetthrottle`, button in `webui/static/app/config.js`). When the fetch queue drains after a pass (the initial fill, or an EPG update that pulled new images), the thread logs `fetch queue drained -- N image(s) fetched, M failed`, so the log shows when caching has caught up (100%). ### Fix a latent use-after-free in `imagecache_destroy()` The fetch queue holds no reference, so destroying a still-queued image (`QUEUED` or pending `SAVE`) freed it and left a dangling `TAILQ` entry the fetch thread later dereferenced (`SIGABRT`). Unlink from the queue before `decref`. Latent in stock tvheadend (a clean/purge racing the fetch thread) but the back-off makes it reproducible: images sit `QUEUED` for the whole pause, so a clean during a pause almost always hits one. Both metadata-save paths (the fetch thread and the on-demand fetch) release the lock to write the meta file; if a concurrent `destroy()` removes the image during that window they now drop the just-written meta file (re-checking `imagecache_by_id` after re-locking), so no orphan metadata survives without its data file. --- Also aligns the existing *"Expire time"* label with the period settings (`(days)`). --- ## Validation — overnight run against a real provider (tvtv.ca) ### Auto-throttle full lifecycle The throttle escalates pauses, **confirms** each candidate pause actually refills the window, then **locks** onto the smallest pause that works — so it converges on a sustainable rate instead of spiralling into ever-longer waits. 21:04:36 [ INFO] auto-throttle: learning provider budget (pacing 250 ms/image until blocked) 21:04:37 [ WARN] auto-throttle: provider blocking -> pausing 5 min 21:09:37 [ WARN] auto-throttle: provider blocking -> pausing 10 min 21:19:39 [ WARN] auto-throttle: provider blocking -> pausing 15 min 21:35:02 [ INFO] auto-throttle: pausing 15 min works (~50 images), confirming 21:50:03 [ WARN] auto-throttle: provider blocking -> pausing 30 min 22:20:03 [ WARN] auto-throttle: provider blocking -> pausing 60 min 23:20:27 [ INFO] auto-throttle: pausing 60 min works (~51 images), confirming 00:20:49 [ INFO] auto-throttle: locked -- budget ~51 images / 60 min -> pacing 70588 ms/image, burst 38 | Phase | Log marker | What it proves | |-------|-----------|----------------| | Learn | `learning provider budget` | Probes at full speed until the first block | | Escalate | `provider blocking -> pausing N min` | Walks the pause ladder (5→10→15→30→60) | | Con

## Descripción
### Contexto
- El archivo `discipline.fullstack.spec.ts` tenía tests secuenciales donde cada test dependía del estado que dejaba el anterior, lo que los hacía frágiles e imposibles de correr de forma independiente.

### Solución implementada
- Se refactorizó `discipline.fullstack.spec.ts` para que cada test sea independiente.
- Se agregó `beforeEach` que crea un socio real via API antes de cada test.
- Se agregó `afterEach` que limpia la sanción y el socio creados después de cada test.
- Los tests de editar y eliminar crean su propia sanción via API antes de correr, sin depender del test anterior.

### Referencia
- TDD-0010 (Alta) / TDD-0011 (Modificación) / TDD-0012 (Eliminación)

---

## Cambios principales
- `beforeEach`: crea un socio real con DNI y email aleatorios para evitar colisiones.
- `afterEach`: elimina la sanción y el socio creados para dejar la DB limpia.
- Tests de editar y eliminar: crean su propia sanción via API antes de interactuar con la UI.

---

## Decisiones técnicas relevantes
- Se usa `request.newContext()` de Playwright para hacer llamadas directas a la API sin pasar por la UI, manteniendo los tests rápidos y precisos.
- El DNI y email del socio se generan con un número aleatorio para evitar colisiones entre ejecuciones.

---

## Testing
### Automatizado
- [ ] `npm run test`
- [ ] `npm run e2e`
- [x] `npm run e2e:fullstack:run`

### Manual
1. Levantar el proyecto con `docker compose up`.
2. Correr `npm run e2e:fullstack:run` desde `packages/web`.
3. Verificar que los 4 tests pasan de forma independiente.

### Resultado esperado
- Los 4 tests E2E fullstack pasan correctamente y cada uno puede correr de forma independiente sin depender del estado del anterior.

---

## Requiere acciones adicionales
- [x] Ninguna

## Dependencias
- [x] No agrega dependencias

---

## Impacto técnico
- [x] Sin impacto relevante

---

## ⚠️ Riesgos / Consideraciones
- Los tests requieren que `docker compose up` esté corriendo con la DB, la API y el frontend levantados.
- El test de "crear sanción" no guarda el id de la sanción creada via UI, por lo que el `afterEach` no la elimina. Esto es aceptable para un test E2E fullstack.

---

- [x] Código revisado por mí

## Overview
Establishes the project's testing approach for the date feature and aligns the existing tests with it. The strategy is two complementary kinds of tests, both in `commonTest` so they run on every target — including the WasmJs target used in CI:

1. **Sociable unit test** at the view-model level (real collaborators, only the system-clock boundary faked).
2. **Integration test** for the faked boundary (CI-runnable).

View-model-level tests are used instead of Compose UI tests because UI node detection on WasmJs is currently unreliable; asserting `uiState` directly avoids that limitation.

## Final test suite (commonTest)
- **`WhatIsTheDateTodayViewModelImplTest`** (sociable): exercises `WhatIsTheDateTodayViewModelImpl` with its real collaborator `CurrentDateRepositoryImpl`, replacing only the clock boundary with `FakeCurrentDateDataSource`. Asserts the `uiState` mapping: every field, all seven day-of-week resources (2024-01-01 Mon … 2024-01-07 Sun), and the Reiwa year (2019 → 1, 2026 → 8).
- **`CurrentDateDataSourceImplTest`** (integration): verifies the real `CurrentDateDataSourceImpl` reports the actual system date; reading control dates before/after tolerates a midnight rollover.
- **`FakeCurrentDateDataSource`**: parameterized hand-written test double (no JVM-only mocking library, so it works on all targets).

- `ComposeAppCommonTest` — wizard placeholder asserting `1 + 2 == 3`.
- `OpenSourceLicensesScreenTest` — a Compose UI test (the avoided kind); also failed on desktop with `MissingResourceException`.
- `CurrentDateRepositoryTest` — a solitary repository test already covered by the sociable view-model test.

- No production code changes — the clock boundary is faked from the test side.

Player-experience pass on the Season tab — **P0: make the draft legible** (chosen from the UI review).

Previously the draft showed raw engine ids (`the_fool`, `aspect_of_ruin`, `Aegis`), so you couldn't make an informed pick. This resolves every draft choice to its display name + a short blurb.

## What changed
- **Draft offers** (characters / items / team passives / banners) render their **display name** plus a one-line description, with the full text on hover:
  - characters → `Cost N · Passive: X — …`
  - items → description + stat bonuses (e.g. `VIT -2, MGT +2`)
  - team passives / banners → the buff description (banner notes its scope)
- **Display names replace slugs** elsewhere: claimed picks in the schedule, the builder's locked-content warnings, and the **opponent in your results** (resolved from standings).
- The client now loads the **team-passive and banner catalogs** (via the embedded WASM catalog, with a fetch fallback) so all four offer kinds resolve.

## Architecture
- New **pure** helpers in `rules-lib.js` — `describeDraftOffer(kind, id, catalogs)` and `formatStatBonuses` — keep name/blurb resolution DOM-free and unit-tested; `app.js` passes the loaded catalogs in.

## Verification
- Tier 1: `node --test tools/ui/tests/*.test.cjs` — **16/16** (2 new).
- Tier 2: `node tools/ui/smoke-test.cjs` — **25/25** (new: offers use display names + show descriptions; claim reflects by display name).
- No engine or server changes.

Follow-ups from the review still on the table (not in this PR): pool-aware team builder, a next-action status strip, host/admin split + auto-refresh.
